method: Two local runs; twelve dictionary width/cardinality/selection cases per run; two warmups and six measured rounds with alternating order. Both paths construct identical row objects. Optional cache directory has exact admission; one-byte shortage uses direct decoding.
findings: All output values match existing vectorValue, including UTF-8 BOM and malformed input replacement.
Repeated dictionary entries reduce decoder calls; unique entries do not.
Cache directory is cardinality-sized even when sparse selection touches few entries. Universal eager caching is unsuitable.
scope: Microbenchmark excludes source/output admission and is not production query, cloud throughput or whole-runtime memory evidence. No production default changed.
next: Investigate bounded lazy reuse sensitive to observed dictionary-index repetition, with cache workspace admitted before allocation and direct access when admission or reuse is insufficient. Preserve independent binary ownership; restrict immutable scalar reuse by explicit vector shape.
